The Body Shop Introduces New Line of Products With Hemp Seed Oil;
Denounced By Tory MP

LONDON

Bath and body care products retailer The Body Shop announced a five-product line formulated with hemp seed oil. While there are a wide variety of such products on the market in the US, the entry of a major international retailer with The Body Shop’s reputation is a major breakthrough for hemp producers.

"Ignorance confuses hemp with marijuana, even though you'd need a joint the size of a telegraph pole to get any kind of buzz,"

Ian Low, director of Hemcore, which has grown hemp in Essex northeast of London said, "It's a rotational crop which is fully grown to 16 feet in only three months, requires virtually no attention, doesn't use pesticides and enriches the soil."

Although the European Union approves the growth of 12 types of hemp seed in Britain, it said last month it may cut aid amid concern that public money was being used to legitimize the cultivation of marijuana.
See

Conservative member of Parliament Ann Widdecombe criticized the products. "It's about making a joke of drug-taking and is wholly irresponsible," she said.

"I keep thinking there are real conspiracies afloat -- it doesn't make rational sense that the benefits this plant can supply are being vilified," Roddick said.  (Ed. note: I think she’s got it!)
